audits.resolution_reason: Unresolved teaching-support gap: 100 sampled source scenes are left-half-only; handcrafted right-origin witness passes validator and actual Racket differs from left-only rival. Distinguish sampled distribution from broader accepted domain.
audits.text:
## 11447f24cd43

**Reproduced teaching shortcut — one-sided source support.** The generator draws
all nonzero source marks from columns `0 .. floor(w/2)-1`. In 100 deterministic
samples it produced zero right-origin marks. Therefore the plausible wrong rule
“keep the input and mirror only marks found in the left half” is identical to the
canonical rule on every generated input, even though the public rule mirrors
marks from either side.

The retained 6×8 counterexample has one color-4 mark at `(2,6)`. It passes the
task's `self_check` but is outside the documented/generated left-half support.
The canonical Racket rule (hash `f48a460c6519`) outputs color 4 at both `(2,6)`
and `(2,1)`; the shortcut keeps only `(2,6)`. The sole differing cell is
`(2,1): actual 4, rival 0`.

Evidence: `checks/audit/11447f24cd43/finding.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`,
and `rival-left-sources-only.json`. Assigned generator SHA:
`a262fb96f901e62069162eafa8fafa5c1a7a0bfee97c9de9122c60105957761a`.
Suggested repair: sample right-only and mixed-side sources, declare the
left-sources-only competitor, and require a per-lesson witness. No audit source
was changed.
